subject: Intermittent 503s on inference endpoint — downtime confirmation & credit request
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@velorafinance.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 503s on inference endpoint — downtime confirmation & credit request

Hi Rachel,

We started seeing a spike of 503 responses on our inference route (model: opt-6b-v2-redwood) this morning around 09:41 PDT. The error rate climbed to ~2.8% between 09:41 and 10:23; we observed elevated tail latency for a subset of requests, and a couple of downstream retries that impacted checkout throughput.

Can you confirm whether Redwood recorded a service availability gap for our tenant during that window and whether Velora Finance is eligible for a pro-rata service credit? We're preparing an internal post-incident summary and would like to know the formal eligibility pathway and any evidence you'll need from us.

I've attached a sample of the client-side traces and request IDs (velora_trace_sample.log) and included a short snippet from our monitoring below.

- Customer impact: intermittent checkout failures for ~42 minutes (roughly 09:41–10:23 PDT)
- Severity: business-impacting (failed checkout attempts)
- Immediate ask: downtime confirmation, estimate of next steps and timeline for credit determination

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Platform Reliability, Velora Finance
Aisha.k@velorafinance.com
[attachment: velora_trace_sample.log (214KB, text)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@velorafinance.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s on inference endpoint — downtime confirmation & credit request

Hi Aisha — thanks for the report and the trace sample.

Short answer: we will evaluate entitlement and perform a formal downtime verification. Next steps from our side:

1) Marcus and the SRE team will pull server-side telemetry (routing, kube events, scaler logs, kernel-level evictions) for the 09:30–10:30 PDT window and assemble a raw trace bundle.
2) We'll compute the availability delta for your tenant using the standard SLO definition in section 4.2 of your agreement and confirm whether the event meets the threshold for a credit.
3) If eligible, we'll propose a pro-rata credit and send a formal remediation summary and postmortem invite.

Could you attach (if available) the approximate revenue affected or a short estimate of failed transactions in that period — that helps us size the pro-rata calc for internal approvals.

I'm attaching our SLA claim form to help structure the request; please return it with any additional request IDs.

Expect an initial evidence packet and preliminary eligibility estimate within 5 business days. Marcus — can you prioritize the trace pull and flag anything that looks like routing fallback or thrashing?

Best,

Rachel Kim
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
[attachment: velora_sla_claim_form_0427.pdf (fillable PDF)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s on inference endpoint — downtime confirmation & credit request

Rachel / team — pulling the traces now. Initial findings (preliminary and subject to correlation):

- Evidence window: 2028-04-27T09:40:42-07:00 → 2028-04-27T10:22:58-07:00 (42m16s)
- Observed symptom: elevated 5xx rate (~2.6–3.1%) across a subset of host shards serving your tenant; concurrent increase in RPC retry latencies.
- Likely cause (initial): a transient autoscaler oscillation coupled with a KV-cache eviction storm on two worker nodes (kube OOM & kernel preemption traces included). This produced a short period of degraded throughput and increased queued requests.

Attachments to follow: velora_trace_bundle_0427.tar.gz (server-side traces, router logs, autoscaler snapshots, kvcache digests).

By our SLA definition (availability computed as successful responses / total requests with business-critical routing), this looks like a material availability delta. I recommend we open an SLA claim flow for Velora Finance and schedule a postmortem; I'll include precise metrics (per-shard failure rate, per-route latency CDFs) in the evidence packet.

Proposed timeline:
- End of day today: raw evidence bundle to Rachel and Aisha
- 2 business days: availability delta calc and eligibility recommendation
- 5 business days: final determination and remediation/postmortem invite

Flagging Laura for any contract edge cases — this event crosses the threshold for a standard credit recommendation, but final approval needs finance sign-off if the credit exceeds the 30-day revenue cap.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[attachment: velora_trace_bundle_0427.tar.gz (7.2MB)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@velorafinance.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s on inference endpoint — downtime confirmation & credit request

Hi Aisha — follow-up and summary of next steps.

We received Marcus's preliminary evidence and are processing the full telemetry bundle. Per our internal thresholds, Velora Finance's tenant shows an availability delta during 09:40–10:23 PDT that is likely to qualify for a pro-rata remedy. We will:  

- Share the raw evidence bundle (link below) and the computed availability delta by EOD Apr 30 (2 business days).  
- Complete a formal eligibility recommendation and finance review within 5 business days (May 4).  
- Convene a joint postmortem (Redwood SRE + Velora ops) in the week following the final determination; I'll propose slots once the team confirms availability.

Next action for you: please return the attached SLA claim form (velora_sla_claim_form_0427.pdf) with any missing request IDs and a short estimate of failed transactions or revenue impact — that will speed finance approval.

HubSpot case: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/VEL-12904  
Evidence bundle (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/velora/0427-traces

Thanks for the quick heads-up — we'll keep this prioritized.

Rachel Kim
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
